svg.text: How far each version got
Slay the Spire 2, Ironclad, Ascension 0, standard runs (no run modifiers). Each dot is one run, green if it won; the bar reaches the best run.
Hollow dots: runs affected by a known issue (see the notes under the table).
Act 1 boss
floor 17
Act 2 boss
floor 33
Final boss
floor 48
Jev only
One compact question per screen, no call for forced moves, reviews on risky end turns
Route and resource facts from code: elites, rests, shops, heal, potions and gold ahead
Ordered route facts; second looks at hallway potion use and leaving a shop with gold
Jev + Claude strategist
Claude writes the run plan at key moments; map moves follow its chosen act route
Enforced combat rules: no fatal play if one survives, potion HP floor, focus target
Claude picks rewards, shop buys, events and rest sites; fight plans saved per encounter
Forecasts for exhaust and finishing cards like Fiend Fire; forecast wins are taken
No ending a turn with a playable Beckon; least HP loss while enemies are Intangible
Moves wait for the game's ready signal instead of fixed delays (about 4x faster)
Briefs add enemy patterns, past card picks and fight results; potions saved for bosses
A second look when Jev's line loses far more HP than the best surviving line
Win forecasts distrust unmodeled debuffs; the boss potion reserve yields at low HP
No healing potion that would mostly overheal; route plans start fresh each run
Incoming-damage forecasts account for Weak and Vulnerable; costly forced plays yield
Frantic Escape forecast; a forced escape yields when it dies and a block line survives
Hallway potions only when the turn would drop HP under the floor; Paper Cuts forecast
Potions with effects the forecast can't show stay usable; briefs name a small draw pile
Fixes for multi-page events and transform screens; no play that starves a held Beckon
Orichalcum forecast; route facts give the fewest elites before the first rest
Asks again before a low-HP route commits to an avoidable elite; guidance on Act 1
rewards, elites and resting
Block cards with scaling or energy-refund text count as pure block on a turn with
nothing incoming
In the last 6 floors before the Act 1 boss, an optional elite only near full HP
Beating the final boss on floor 48 wins the run. Early strategist versions reused seed JEV1 (v3.1 to v3.3 replayed v3's non-combat choices on it);
from v3.5 on, every run uses a new seed.
The imported Jev the Spire policy reached the Act 3 boss once, in a Hextech Mayhem run. That modifier changes the game, so the run is not plotted.
Runs still in progress are not plotted.
